no_cutoff._about: JP, 2026-11-27: no paper is ever cut off. Ladder for every LLM stage (picost, recheck, adjudicate, checks, drafts, qs, src), implemented in scripts/lives_stages.py (cutoff_ladder): (1) the request ends with MAX_TOKENS, max_tokens, CONTINUATION, incomplete or length; (2) it is sent again in the same mode (batch stays the rule) at medium thinking effort (low if it was already medium) with the largest output budget of its model; (3) if that is cut off too, it is sent again in standard (non-batch) mode with the largest budget and the retry is marked in the manifest (cutoff_retries); (4) if that is cut off as well, the request is marked needs JP (manifest needs_jp; a paper-level stage stops that paper with status needs JP) and does not count toward the 'two or more papers failed' stop. Budget basis: the largest paper of the 27-paper seed set (sysrev/dgraph/source/pdfs, measured with PyMuPDF on 2026-11-27) is Liu and Shah 2023 (ReviewerGPT) with 60 pages; the largest by text is D'Arcy 2024 (MARG) with 52 pages and 217,751 characters (about 62,000 tokens at 3.5 characters per token). Input at this pipeline's 1,400 tokens per page is 60 x 1,400 = 84,000 tokens, which fits every context window used. Output is the problem, not input: thinking tokens count against the output budget, and Woelfle (11 pages) already used more than 67,000 at high thinking, so no per-page formula reaches the need of a 60-page paper. The budget is therefore the model limit for every paper, and the ladder carries the rest.
steps: same mode at medium effort and the model's largest budget
standard mode at the model's largest budget

project_question: In benchmarking experiments, how accurately, quickly, and cost-effectively can Large Language Models (LLMs), Pretrained Language Models (PLMs), other NLP models, fine-tuned systems, and AI agents evaluate scholarly abstracts, preprints, and full research reports (including journal articles, conference proceedings, scholarly coursework, research proposals and ethics-review materials), across broad tasks such as peer review and narrower tasks such as error and limitation detection, critical appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, reporting-guideline compliance, claim checking, novelty assessment, replicability prediction, ethics and style compliance, protocol and registration concordance, plagiarism and duplicate-publication detection, and distinguishing human-written from AI-generated scholarly writing? Evidence: empirical comparisons of AI judgments against human experts or another reference standard with quantitative results, plus time and cost where reported.

writing._about: EVD writing-rules check (JP, 2026-11-26): all-caps words of four or more letters are flagged unless listed here (names of tools, models and metrics).

quality_signals._about: JP, 2026-11-27 (procedure pending validation): one rater (roles.raters, Gemini 4 Neon high) rates every quality-signal and TRIPOD-LLM row and reports a confidence (high, medium, low). A rating with low confidence goes to the fallback rater (roles.qs_fallback, GPT-6.2 Sol high); if the fallback is also low confidence the row is marked needs_human for JP. The verification cascade is not bypassed. Set max_accuracy to true (with three entries in roles.raters) for the earlier maximum-accuracy mode: three raters, a rating needs two of three, every verifier judges every rating.
